pride-lodge.title: Pride Lodge, Blackpool: gay guest house
pride-lodge.description: A mixed LGBTQ+ stay near the station: Pride Lodge offers a guest sauna, gym and garden hot tub in season, with the Flying Handbag around the corner.
pride-lodge.h1: Staying at Pride Lodge: a welcoming gay guest house by Blackpool North
pride-lodge.intro: Pride Lodge is an all-welcome LGBTQ+ guest house near Blackpool North, with a guest sauna and gym and an easy walk to the Queen Street and Dickson Road bars.
pride-lodge.body_html:
Who is Pride Lodge best for?

Pride Lodge is the one to pick if you want somewhere friendly and sociable but not rowdy. The house says all are welcome rather than limiting itself to men, so couples, mixed friend groups and solo travellers all fit.

You will find it among the older guest-house streets between the station and Dickson Road. Arriving by train is simple, and Funny Girls and the Flying Handbag are both close by.

Rooms and facilities

Inside, expect:

  • An in-room smart TV and fridge, with a light breakfast brought to the room
  • Guest use of the sauna, a sunbed and the gym
  • An outdoor hot tub from about April to early October
  • A local-venues discount card, plus standing tickets for Funny Girls
  • Cut-price Banks Street car park passes from reception

Is Pride Lodge men-only or adults-only?

It presents itself as mixed and welcoming to everyone, not men-only. Nothing we hold confirms an adults-only rule, so ask if children are coming along.

Your nearest options from Pride Lodge:

  • Rendezvous Bar and Rooms, 1 min away: a small, friendly bar with rooms at the station end of Lord Street.
  • The Flying Handbag, 1 min away: a big Queen Street bar and club with drag hosts, karaoke and a sun terrace.
  • Funny Girls, 2 mins away: drag cabaret in a restored art deco cinema, with listed show nights Wednesday to Sunday.

Hours change, so see what is open tonight before you head out. For the full venue background, see the Rainbow Quarter directory.

From Blackpool North it is about 1 min on foot, so you can arrive by train and be checked in quickly. The Prom at North Pier is 9 mins away and the Tower is 12 mins, so a sea-air stroll before dinner is easy to fit in. The safety guide has sensible tips for getting home after dark.

Is it the right fit?

A mixed LGBTQ+ stay is the easiest option for friends who want a welcoming base without a single rule for everyone. If Pride Lodge is full or not quite right, the nearest alternatives by walking time are Q Accommodation, Mardi Gras, Trades Hotel and Bar; the stays directory compares them all.

Booking tips

Event weekends carry a minimum of three nights, while midweek visits of two nights or longer can earn a reduction. Reception is manned 10am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and 11am to 5pm Sunday, with WhatsApp outside those hours, so message if your train is late.

Rooms go early for Blackpool Pride and the Illuminations, so book as soon as you know your dates. Prices and availability change, so always check the venue's own site or phone before you pay: https://www.pridelodge.com/.

  • Buy your parking pass at reception before you park
  • Sauna, gym and hot tub details come from the owner-checked listing; confirm what is open when you book
  • Our extra research could not independently verify the facilities, so check the guest house site

It suits couples and small groups who want a sociable bar downstairs and a room to retreat to. It sits further along Lord Street than the station-end houses, so expect a longer walk from the train and the Dickson Road venues.

  • Each en-suite room has its own theme
  • A breakfast that guests speak well of
  • A bar that non-residents can use, with cocktail offers, weekend happy hours and food

  • Roast dinners on Sundays, booking required

Group, stag and hen bookings are refused outright, which tells you most of what you need to know: it is for couples and small friend groups wanting the bars nearby but a hush at bedtime.

Phoenix is gay-owned but described as gay-friendly rather than exclusively gay, so the mix of guests is relaxed. It sits right in the heart of the quarter, which means the bars are a few steps away and the walk home is short.

The rules shape who it suits. It is 18+, does not take stag or hen parties, and does not accept under-25s at weekends. Quiet hours start at 11pm. Think couples and friends who want a good night out and a proper sleep afterwards.

Because the house is small, a booking here feels more personal than a big hotel. Ask what suits your party before you commit: its rules are clear, and knowing them in advance avoids awkwardness on arrival.

Guests who want a cooked breakfast can find one at a diner a few steps away, so you are not stuck with the light continental offer if you want something bigger before a day on the Prom.

Does Phoenix Guest House take stag and hen parties?

It is mixed rather than men-only, so it suits couples and friends alike. Pride weekend bookings are reportedly taken by phone so the house can build a lively, very gay atmosphere.

Because it sits right on Dickson Road, you can walk to Funny Girls and the neighbouring bars in moments, then come back to a proper cooked breakfast the next morning.

Rooms are heated and en suite, so it works in the colder months as well as summer, and the Illuminations season is a good time to visit if you like the lights.

  • Central heating
  • Tea and coffee and toiletries
